title: Sectional Cutoff Strategies
tagline: Year 4 — Meeting both sectional and overall cutoffs: allocating effort, computing minimum marks and avoiding a failing section

introduction.overview: Some assessments require a minimum score in each section as well as overall. A strong total can then still fail you if one section falls below its cutoff. The strategy is to compute the minimum marks you need in each section, secure them first, and use the remaining effort where your marks per minute are highest. This chapter practises the arithmetic of cutoffs and the logic of balance; All figures and rules in this chapter's examples are hypothetical teaching examples and are not the rules of any real company or platform; always read the official instructions.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sectional cutoffs are common and filter candidates who neglect a weak section.
introduction.realWorldContext: Meeting minimum requirements in every component is how many qualifications work.

learningObjectives: Compute sectional and overall cutoffs in marks
Find the minimum marks needed in the last section
Avoid failing a section by neglect
Check the feasibility of a target

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Cutoff marks = percentage × section marks. Marks needed in the last section = overall target − marks already earned.

coreDefinitions: Sectional cutoff: minimum marks in a section.
Feasibility: whether the target can be met.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A chain is as strong as its weakest link; a sectional cutoff makes the weakest section decisive.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Compute each cutoff in marks, secure the weakest section first, and top up elsewhere.

mainNarrative: Suppose (hypothetically) sections of 20, 15 and 25 marks with a 40% sectional cutoff and a 60% overall cutoff. Sectional cutoffs in marks: 8, 6 and 10; the overall cutoff is 36 of 60.
If you earn 14 in Aptitude and 7 in Reasoning, you have 21; you need at least 15 in Verbal to reach 36 (more than the 10 sectional minimum), which is feasible since Verbal has 25 marks.
If Reasoning is your weak section, secure its 6 marks first; losing a whole section to a cutoff is worse than losing a few marks elsewhere.
Margins help: aim a few marks above each cutoff to absorb mistakes.

deepDiveAspects.title: Strategic neglect
deepDiveAspects.content: Skipping a weak section entirely risks failing the sectional cutoff even if the total is high.

deepDiveAspects.title: Overall target depends on penalties
deepDiveAspects.content: If wrong answers cost marks, count net marks.

solvedExamples.title: Cutoff marks
solvedExamples.question: A 40% sectional cutoff on a 20-mark section is how many marks?

solvedExamples.title: Needed last
solvedExamples.question: Overall cutoff 36. You have 14 + 7 = 21. Marks needed in the last section?

solvedExamples.title: Feasibility
solvedExamples.question: The last section has 25 marks and you need 15. Is it feasible?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Yes, it requires 60% of that section

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Compute each cutoff in marks, secure the weakest section first, then top up where your rate is highest.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I convert cutoffs to marks?
